title: Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor
summary: In 1971 Intel introduced the 4004, advertised that November as the first commercially available microprocessor. It began as a contract for the Japanese calculator company Busicom, when Ted Hoff proposed a general-purpose 4-bit computer on four chips. Federico Faggin, assisted by Masatoshi Shima, fitted its 2,300 transistors onto one chip using silicon-gate technology. In May 1971 Intel bought back the rights for uses beyond calculators.

uncertainty.note: Commercial release of the MCS-4 family including the 4004 central processing unit in 1971.

as_recorded.value: They introduced this groundbreaking microcomputer chip family to the world in 1971 as the MCS-4 Micro Computer Set
